'Be the best you can be'
Welcome to our website!
At Hagbourne, we have a committed staff who work hard to provide a safe, caring and nurturing environment with exciting learning opportunities. Within our Christian ethos we foster a love of learning along with developing a ‘toolkit’ of strategies, knowledge and understanding to prepare our children for the opportunities, challenge, responsibilities and experiences of life. We encourage them to overcome difficulties and see mistakes as a vital part of the the learning journey.

Governance Information
Hagbourne Church of England Primary School joined the Ridgeway Education Trust (RET) on 1st May 2024, as an academy school in part of the wider Multi Academy Trust (MAT).
Ridgeway Education Trust is run by a Board of Directors which has ultimate responsibility for running each academy within its structure and for setting the vision for schools within the MAT. You can find out more about Governance in the Trust by clicking this link.
Each school retains its own Local Governing Body which includes representatives from the Church, staff, parents and members of the local community appointed for their particular skills and experience.
The schools in the MAT share the core values of high-quality teaching and learning, respectful relationships and an inclusive community. These underpin the Trust’s continuing development and support its commitment to excellence.
The Local Governing Body meets as a whole at least five times a year, and is focused on setting the School’s values, vision and strategic aims, agreeing plans and policies and making creative use of our resources. The role of the governors is to provide the best possible education for their pupils by:
Our Governors are all volunteers and are willing to use their individual skills to collectively support the work of the school. Each member of the Governing Board attends Full Governing Board meetings and are responsible for monitoring their particular area and feeding back to the main body.
Minutes of Governors meetings
Minutes of the governors meetings can be obtained by contacting the school office or RET Governance Team on Governance@ridgewayeducation.com

pageCache.text:
Music lessons and groups
At Hagbourne, we have a number of peripatetic teachers offering instrument through Oxfordshire Music Service. We also have private piano lessons available, iRock and our school choir.
If your child is interested in learning an instrument, further details on how to apply for lessons through OMS are available in the letter below, including details on how to check if you are eligible for free instrumental lessons and hire.
Instrumental tuition
If your child wishes to learn an instrument they can sign up for lessons with Oxfordshire Music Service (OMS). Please visit their website and sign up online by clicking the link below.
They offer lessons in:
Current price (from Sep 2025)
Number in group/length of lesson
If only one pupil applies for a group lesson, they will stay on the waiting list until a group can be formed. Applicants can opt for an individual lesson.
Families may be entitled to free lessons, ensemble membership and instrument hire if you are in receipt of one of the following benefits.
Universal Credit with an annual net earned income of no more than £7,400.
Income-based Jobseeker’s Allowance
Income-related Employment and Support Allowance
Support under Part 6 of the Immigration and Asylum Act 1999
The guarantee element of Pension Credit
Working Tax Credit run-on (paid for the four weeks after you stop qualifying for Working Tax Credit)
Child Tax Credit (with no Working Tax Credit) with an annual income of no more than £16,190
Please be aware that entitlement to Free School Meals does not guarantee entitlement for free music lessons. You may be liable for the cost of lessons if your entitlement is not confirmed.
The school works with a private piano teacher who sometimes has spaces available throughout the school year. Please contact the office if you are interested and we can ask to have your name put on the waiting list if no spaces are available.
We also host iRock lessons where children form bands and become a keyboard player, a guitarist, a vocalist or a drummer. This is fantastic for both coordination, musical knowledge, confidence and team work. Follow the link to enrol your child https://www.irockschool.com/enrol
The Hagbourne School Choir is open to children in KS2 and they rehearse every Thursday after school. The choir have previously sung in Oxford, taken part in Young Voices as well as leading our school carol service and other local events. If your child is interested in joining the choir, please contact the school office.

SEND
At Hagbourne CE School we are committed to helping every child 'be the best they can be'. We recognise that every single child is different, with their own unique talents. We know that children come to school with different strengths and experiences and at some point, many children may find some aspects of school challenging. These may be academic, social, behavioural or emotional challenges. At our school, we share an inclusive ethos and a commitment to supporting all children.
To find out more about how we support all children to 'be the best they can be' through our Inclusive Provision at Hagbourne, please see our SEND Information Report below.
A child has a learning difficulty or disability if he or she:
(Code of Practice DfE 2014)
The school will follow the guidance contained within the Oxfordshire County Council document Identifying and Supporting Special Educational Needs (OCC 2014).
Where learners are not making expected progress and are significantly behind their peers, evidence is gathered from school, home and the learner him/herself to make a detailed assessment of need and put in place appropriate support. For those with the most complex needs, an Education Health and Care (EHC) plan will be agreed.
In accordance with legal requirements, children who have an Educational, Health and Care Plan naming the school in that plan will always be admitted. Children with disabilities who need to be admitted to a school on the grounds of physical accessibility have a priority in the school’s Admissions Policy. Please see our school admissions page for more details.
In its day to day operation, the school will work to:
The school has an accessibility plan showing how it plans to evaluate and improve access to all aspects of the school and school life.
This provision supports the local offer of Oxfordshire County Council. See below for the link to this.
Our vision for children and young people with special needs is the same as for all children and young people – that they achieve well in their early years and at school; lead happy and fulfilled lives; and have choice and control. (Oxfordshire County Council)
Staff at Hagbourne are committed to ensuring that our school is a fully inclusive, happy environment where children are nurtured and supported to achieve excellence. As such, children are offered the same opportunities and included in all school activities regardless of their area of additional need.
What does inclusive learning look like at Hagbourne?
Special Educational Needs Staff
Our Special Educational Needs Coordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Jo Hudson.
Our SEND link Governors are Joanna Passey and Steve Nicholson.
We have two Nurture & Emotional Support Teaching Assistants – Anna Breeze and Carrie Jones.
If you ever have any questions, queries or concerns about your child, please do not hesitate to talk to our SENDCo or Headteacher. Just ring the office to make an appointment.
If you have any complaints about the school's SEND support for your child, then please contact our SENDCo or the Headteacher. If after this, you feel that it has not been resolved, then please follow the school's complaint procedure.

Curriculum
Our aim is to provide an inspiring curriculum and environment that ignites a love of learning and educates all children to excel as individuals. Our curriculum is intended to:
Our curriculum is carefully designed to ensure clear progression in skills and knowledge from Reception to Year 6, preparing children for the next stage of their learning. Learning builds on prior knowledge to create depth and support long term retention. Long term curriculum planning is reviewed regularly by teaching staff and subject leaders, pupils contribute to the design and evaluation of learning, and we reflect continually on research and best practice to improve teaching and learning

PTA
Welcome to the PTA section.
Hagbourne CE School PTA
Here at Hagbourne the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) is made up of three Trustees, these Trustees are all parents of children at the school:
Chair – Natalie Wood
Treasurer – Leanne Longland
Secretary – Dominique McCann
The Trustees are also supported by a wider team, also all parents from the school, Laura Lloyd, Katherine Adams, Sophie Garland and Jessica Wells.
The PTA is a registered charity and has an elected committee of three parents to act as Chair, Secretary, and Treasurer. The PTA meets every term to discuss issues affecting parents at the school and upcoming events organised by the PTA.
What does the PTA do?
The PTA meet every term to discuss issues affecting parents at the school and organise and plan events to fundraise for the school. Examples of events that the PTA organise and run include discos for the children and second-hand uniform sale. They also put on other events both for social and for fundraising.
Through the PTA, Hagbourne parents and carers have raised thousands of pounds and provided the school with much-needed resources. In recent years the money raised has helped the school;
How can I get involved?
At Hagbourne, we are lucky to have an active, committed and hardworking Parent-Teacher Association (PTA). However, we do always welcome new members – all parents of children in the school are automatically members of the PTA, but if you would like to contribute ideas, make suggestions, or help with planning and running our events, please get in touch.
You can find the dates of our upcoming meetings below, please reach out if you would like to join us:
Facebook https://www.facebook.com/groups/ptahagbourne/
Email hagbourneschoolpta@gmail.com
If you see us around school, come up and say hello!
